sources_considered.why: Meta's primary launch post for Llama 4 (April 2025). It describes text and vision input only.
News report from the post date. It says OpenAI, Google, xAI and now Anthropic offer voice chat, and that Claude voice mode handles images.
OpenAI's primary post saying GPT-4o accepts text, audio, image and video input. Dated 2024, so used as context.
Google's primary post saying Gemini 2.0 Flash accepts image, video and audio input. Dated December 2024, so used as context.
Report suggesting Anthropic had not trained its own audio models and relies on ElevenLabs for speech. Context on whether Claude's voice is native.

evidence_items.locator: section on pre-training, paragraph on native multimodality

receipt.public_excerpt: Llama 4 models are designed with native multimodality, incorporating early fusion to seamlessly integrate text and vision tokens into a unified model backbone.

evidence_items.explanation: Meta describes Llama 4, its flagship model at the time, as combining text and vision only. Audio input is not mentioned. So one leading model family accepted images but not audio.

receipt.public_excerpt: A number of AI companies, including OpenAI, offer voice chat experiences for their respective chatbots. Google, for example, has Gemini Live, while xAI has Voice Mode for Grok.

evidence_items.explanation: On the post date, OpenAI, Google and xAI chatbots offered voice input, and Anthropic began rolling out voice mode. The same article says Claude voice users can chat about images. This supports the claim at the chatbot-product level.

receipt.public_excerpt: it accepts as input any combination of text, audio, image, and video and generates any combination of text, audio, and image outputs.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows OpenAI's main model natively took audio and image input from 2024. This fits the claim for OpenAI, but the source is dated before the target period.

receipt.public_excerpt: In addition to supporting multimodal inputs like images, video and audio, 2.0 Flash now supports multimodal output

evidence_items.explanation: Shows Google's Gemini natively took image and audio input from December 2024. This fits the claim for Google, but the source is dated before the target period.

receipt.public_excerpt: This suggests that, unlike OpenAI or Google, Anthropic either hasn't trained its own models on audio or hasn't achieved the necessary quality for speech synthesis on its own.

evidence_items.explanation: Suggests Claude's voice features rely on third-party speech technology rather than native audio in the model. The evidence concerns speech output and is an inference, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: I found no primary Anthropic document from May 2025 saying whether Claude models accepted raw audio. The 2026 docs say text and image input only.
I found no primary DeepSeek document on R1/V3 input types. Secondary sources say they were text-only.
I did not establish whether Grok 3 took audio natively or through speech-to-text.
